subject: NexaCare dedicated fleet commissioning — mutual action plan & fallback sizing
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@nexacare.ai>, NexaCare Infra Team <infra@nexacare.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NexaCare dedicated fleet commissioning — initial mutual action plan

Hi James / Infra team,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our call, I've put together a short mutual action plan (MAP) to get the dedicated GPU fleet commissioned for NexaCare's inference workload. Key points below — I attached a one-page map (nexacare-mvp-map.xlsx) that lays out the phases.

Primary goals
- Get a committed pool in us-west-2 sized for initial traffic (baseline + expected peak for MVP).
- Define autoscale & burst guardrail policy to avoid noisy neighbor cost spikes.
- Establish regional fallback (us-east-1) and cold/warm cache strategy for KV warmup.

Suggested starting config (proposed)
- Phase 1 (MVP): 6 x A100 equivalent GPUs in a single pool (us-west-2) with 20% reserved burst buffer.
- Autoscale: target CPU/GPU lane-based scaling with token-per-request thresholds; warm pool floor = 2 GPUs, scale step = 1 GPU, safety cap = 12 GPUs.
- Burst policy: allow +30% short-term burst for 10 minutes, with automatic fallback to smaller model variant if sustained beyond 10 minutes.
- KV cache warmup: prefix pre-warm for heavy prompt families; recommend a 30 minute warm window pre-cutover.

Open asks for NexaCare
1) Confirm primary region preference (we proposed us-west-2).
2) Confirm acceptable warm/cold caching RTO and risk tolerance for model fallbacks.
3) Provide SOC2 evidence contact for security questionnaire (we will need a SOC2 attestation copy).

Internal CC: Monica — can you drive the SOW and cost calc? Ben — will coordinate netops turn-up and cross-region VPN.

Attachments: nexacare-mvp-map.xlsx (MAP), placeholder for sizing table.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: James Li <james.li@nexacare.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaCare Infra Team <infra@nexacare.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare dedicated fleet commissioning — initial mutual action plan

Connor — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick responses from our side:

1) Region: us-west-2 is fine as primary. We also run some other workloads in us-east-1 and would prefer that as the failover region.
2) Sizing: we want to start smaller than your Phase 1 ask — can we begin with 4 A100 equivalents and validate for 2 weeks? If stable, scale to 8. This helps our initial budget constraints.
3) Autoscale: the idea of a burst buffer is good. Can you provide a cost delta if the buffer is 20% vs 30%?
4) SOC2: please send the checklist and we will route to our compliance contact (sarah.kim@nexacare.ai).

We also have a procurement constraint — all platform charges must be approved by finance prior to any committed capacity. I can route the SOW once you send a formal estimate.

If you can update the MAP with a 4->8 scale plan and an estimated monthly cost band, we'll be ready to review internally this week.

Thanks,
James
James Li
CTO, NexaCare
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: NexaCare MAP — internal implementation questions (please advise)

Forwarding James' reply — see inline notes and internal asks below.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: James Li <james.li@nexacare.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NexaCare dedicated fleet commissioning — initial mutual action plan
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: NexaCare Infra Team <infra@nexacare.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Connor — thanks for the clear plan...

Internal notes (Monica):
- James wants 4->8 ramp, prefer to support that with an initial canary policy rather than straight floor change.
- Procurement will require a monthly estimate for committed capacity; I'll prepare a conservative and an optimistic band.
- Need confirmation from Karthik on autoscale semantics/controls and what telemetry hooks we must expose to NexaCare for SLO dashboards.

Karthik — can you confirm the following by EOD today?
A) Autoscale trigger keys we support (tokens/sec, queue-length, GPU-util). Which would you recommend for NexaCare's expected traffic shape?
B) Can we set a hard reserve (20%) as a pool-level soft-floor that prevents eviction during bursts? How does that interact with our fallback policies?
C) Canary rollout plan: propose a 6-hour canary with gradual qps ramp (25%/50%/100%), and a rollback threshold of error-rate + latency delta. Is that workable?

Ben — please outline netops tasks for cross-region connectivity and estimated lead time.

Thanks — Monica
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: James Li <james.li@nexacare.ai>, NexaCare Infra Team <infra@nexacare.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: NexaCare dedicated fleet commissioning — updated MAP and next steps

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps based on today's internal confirmation:

Agreed commissioning plan
- Initial committed pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (us-west-2). Growth to 8 GPUs if stable after 14 days.
- Regional failover: us-east-1 with cold-standby and KV cache warmup strategy (30-min pre-warm window on cutover).
- Autoscale & burst: pool-level soft-floor = 20% reserved (prevents eviction for short bursts). Short-term burst allowance +30% for up to 10 minutes. Fallback: automatic routing to a quantized smaller model variant if sustained beyond 10 minutes or if pool hits safety cap.
- Canary rollout: 6-hour canary, traffic ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback on >3% error-rate delta or >200ms median latency regression.

Actions and owners
- Redwood (Monica): SOW and monthly estimate (conservative / optimistic bands) due 2027-07-29. Attachment: fleet-sizing-proposal.pdf (estimates).
- NexaCare (James): confirm procurement timeline and SOC2 contact (sarah.kim@nexacare.ai) by 2027-07-28.
- Redwood (Ben): netops runbook for cross-region VPN + routing, list of required VPC peering/firewall openings by 2027-07-30.
- Redwood (Karthik): confirm exact autoscale trigger names and telemetry hooks; provide sample Prometheus metrics and SLO dashboard fields by 2027-07-29.
- Joint: schedule canary cutover window (target week of 2027-08-08) — propose Tue 2027-08-09 02:00-08:00 UTC.

Links and references
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/78421/deal/DEAL-78421
- Draft SOW/DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/samples/sow/DEAL-78421
- Implementation checklist: https://docs.redwood.com/implementation/templates/pool-commissioning-checklist

Attachments: fleet-sizing-proposal.pdf (detailed cost bands and timelines).

If that all looks good James, we'll queue up the SOW and estimation and follow the canary schedule once procurement clears. Happy to hop on a 20-min sync to run through the netops checklist.

Best,
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
